result: h07. **Request path: `GET /file/users/{username}/avatar`** The URL itself comes from the API: `convertUserFromStore` replaces a base64 avatar with a pointer URL so user responses stay small, and the browser's `` uses that value. ``` UserAvatar (img src={avatarUrl}) — web/src/components/UserAvatar.tsx:14 convertUserFromStore (mints "/file/{users/}/avatar") — server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go:36 ``` **Serving handler → data layer:** ``` FileServerService.RegisterRoutes (route: GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:124 FileServerService.serveUserAvatar — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168 FileServerService.getCurrentUser — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:708 [only when !Profile.AllowAnonymous()] Authenticator.AuthenticateToUser — server/auth/authenticator.go:190 [same branch] FileServerService.getUserByUsername — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715 Store.GetUser — store/user.go:148 Store.ListUsers — store/user.go:136 Driver.ListUsers (interface) — store/driver.go:47 (sqlite) DB.ListUsers — store/db/sqlite/user.go:88 (SELECT ... avatar_url ... FROM user WHERE username = ?) also: store/db/mysql/user.go, store/db/postgres/user.go; driver picked in store/db/db.go:14 FileServerService.parseDataURI — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:737 ``` Notes worth flagging: - **The image bytes never leave the database.** The avatar is stored inline in the `user.avatar_url` column as a `data:;base64,...` URI (regex at `fileserver.go:93`), so the last hop is decoding that string — there is no filesystem/S3 hop like attachments have. `parseDataURI` returns the bytes, they're MIME-checked against `avatarAllowedTypes` (`fileserver.go:73`), and written with `c.Blob` under `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600` plus the security headers from `setSecurityHeaders`. - **Cache is bypassed here.** `Store.GetUser` only consults `userCache` when `find.ID` is set (`store/user.go:149`); this lookup is by `Username`, so it always falls through to `ListUsers` and hits SQL — though the fetched row is then written into the cache by ID. - **Authorization is instance-wide, not per-user.** Any other user's avatar is served to any viewer; the only gate is that on a private instance (no `InstanceURL` → `Profile.AllowAnonymous()` false) the requester must authenticate.
